title: MZ Plugin that allows for custom collisions?

posts.author: RomRabbit
posts.body:
Hi! I've recently started using RPG Maker a week or two ago after switching away from Gamemaker due to finding it too difficult (seeing how I'm mainly just an artist first).
I've gotten the basics of the engine down but one thing I've been kinda annoyed with is the collisions being based off of the grid which i feel is kinda limiting. I was wondering if MZ has any good plugins that can let you map out the collisions for sprites in your tileset in a similar way to how Gamemaker's collisions works, sorta like the example below.
Any help with this would be very appreciated, even if its a bit different from what I have in mind!!

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
If GameMaker is too hard you should try GDevelop, not RPG Maker. It is one of the easiest general engines and I've seen children make games with it.
Custom collisions in RPG Maker require plugins, are limited in the size and shapes you can draw, are not intuitive to use, and you won't be able to see them working in the editor. In Gdevelop you can literally draw any collision shapes you want directly in the engine and freely drag and drop it anywhere on the game scene (not stuck to a grid), no plugin needed.
If you insist on using RPG Maker I recommend Tyruswoo's MZ port of Altimit. It's as good as you're going to get for RPG Maker.
Tyruswoo Altimit Movement MZ | Tyruswoo Studio
Plugin for RPG Maker MZ. Add pixel movement to your game! Includes a command to recalculate tile boundaries, for compatibility with Tile Control MZ!
www.tyruswoo.com
RPG Maker is a specialized engine for making (grid-based, turn-based) RPGs. GameMaker is a general purpose engine with a lot more flexibility in game design and mechanics. Your first intuition should be to try an easier general purpose engine with similar flexibility, not move to a specialized tool for a specific genre. There are plugins to allow other mechanics in RPG Maker, but the result will be clunkier, less performant, and sometimes more expensive (if it's a paid plugin) than using the general purpose engine.
